title: Семейный разговор в кабинете  (Family Talk in the Office)

segments.t: Chef Viktor Barinov proudly shows his daughter Katya around his new office at the Italian restaurant Arcobaleno. Katya casually asks her father to hire her, sparking a prickly family argument about why neither of them stayed in touch over the past year.
Я тебя и дольше не видела.
У меня всегда были свои причины.
Шеф, там картошку и помидоры привезли.
Let's examine the tense father-daughter conversation between Chef Barinov and Katya.
'Here are my new apartments.' Barinov holds a natural rhythm at this moment, linking "novyye" ("new"), "apartamenty" ("apartments"), and "vot" ("there, here") in one brisk exchange.
'It is very cozy here in your place.' Katya adopts an emphatic rhythm at once, combining "zdes" ("here") and "ochen" ("very much") so the key meaning lands right away.

'Previously this office belonged to a woman.' Barinov shows a wry tack in front of Katya, pairing "ranshe" ("earlier, previously") with "kabinet" ("office") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'I see you have already settled in.' Katya takes a direct direction in the room, leaning on "smotryu" ("look") before closing the thought with "uzhe" ("already, now").
'Of course, tell me how your life is.' Barinov holds a grounded note in the scene, joining "konechno" ("of course") to "rasskazyvay" ("tell") so every word pulls its weight.
'I am currently looking for a new job.' Katya chooses a candid attitude in the conversation, pairing "seychas" ("now") with "ishchu" ("am looking for") so the "-sya" ending carries the action.
'Dad, will you hire me to work with you?' Katya inquires directly in the room, building the phrase around "papa" ("Dad") and "vozmyosh" ("to take") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'You did not call for a whole year!' Barinov adopts a firm tone at this moment, combining "tselyy" ("whole, all") and "god" ("year") so the key meaning lands right away.

'I have gone even longer without seeing you.' Katya chooses a warm tempo in their talk, leaning on "dolshe" ("take") before closing the thought with "videla" ("saw").

'I always had my own reasons.' Barinov chooses a calm tone as the scene unfolds, joining "vsegda" ("always") to "byli" ("be") so every word pulls its weight.
